subject: built/cueva-de-las-manos
prompt:
ONE landscape 3:2 architectural field-sketchbook page. Clearly visible loose graphite construction lines, quick sepia ink and parallel hatching, restrained uneven watercolor washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue. Detail concentrated on the named structure; irregular unfinished edges fade into bare warm cream paper. An observed hand-drawn working sketch, NOT a photograph, glossy painting, digital render, fantasy concept art or infographic. One coherent perspective, believable load-bearing geometry and consistent scale. No border, binding, labels, captions, date, signature, watermark or readable text. Only tiny indistinct marks for inscriptions. No modern tourism infrastructure unless explicitly part of scene. People optional, small and appropriate to depicted date, never obligatory foreground explorer.

This picture: Shallow rock-shelter overhang high on a pale volcanic cliff above the dry Pinturas river canyon in Patagonian steppe, its wall crowded with overlapping negative hand stencils in red, ochre, black and white, mostly left hands, with small red guanacos and tiny stick-figure hunters closing round them with spears and bolas (no bows) beside them; tufts of grey-green steppe grass below, the canyon floor far beneath; no modern walkways, railings, signs or fences.
